description: The canonical RFC 1035 §4.1 DNS query for example.com A — a 29-byte message: 12-byte header (ID 0x1234, flags 0x0100 = RD set, QDCOUNT 1), then the QNAME as length-prefixed labels (07 'example' 03 'com' 00), QTYPE 1 (A), QCLASS 1 (IN). This is the PEEL exemplar: select QDCOUNT, decode the QNAME labels, read QTYPE/QCLASS.

provenance.built_with: python3 struct.pack of the RFC 1035 §4.1 header + length-prefixed QNAME, this session (2026-06-13)
provenance.verified_against: dig +qr +question example.com A — dig's parsed question reads `;example.com. IN A`, identical to this message's decode (QNAME=example.com, QTYPE=A, QCLASS=IN). A learner can paste the QNAME bytes 076578616d706c6503636f6d00 and decode them by hand to example.com.
provenance.honesty_note: Authored from the RFC with the citation because dig does not emit raw query wire bytes; every field is the RFC-fixed value and the decode matches dig's question section. The 29-byte length and the QNAME label decode are reproducible.
